note: TEACHING MDP for AiM Lecture 6 (reinforcement learning). All transition probabilities, rewards and the clinician policy are ILLUSTRATIVE, chosen by hand for teaching; they are NOT clinical estimates and come from no dataset. One step = 4 hours (as in Komorowski et al., Nat Med 2018). Terminal rewards +R (discharged alive) / -R (died) mirror that paper's +/-100 at 90 days.
transitionFormat: P[state][action] = [p(better), p(same), p(worse)]; 'better' from stable = discharged, 'worse' from refractory shock = died

clinicianPolicy.note: Illustrative stochastic 'behaviour' policy used to simulate records: rows = states, columns = actions (wait, fluids, fluids + vasopressor).
